title: POC Weekly Caching Sync - PulseHealth
summary: Weekly POC sync to review current cache hit rates and discuss tuning & prompt reuse strategies. Current metrics: prefix cache ~23% hit, KV cache ~58% hit. Discussed canonicalization of prompts, TTLs, cache key strategy, and plan to run a constrained benchmark with prefix-only caching and increased KV capacity. Agreed to monitor quality regressions before aggressive caching and to share updated dashboards and docs.
action_items: Samir - Share cache tuning doc and sample canonicalization script - due 2026-09-10
Lena - Run 2-node benchmark with prefix-only caching and 30% increased KV capacity, collect token-level latency/cost - due 2026-09-14
Rajiv - Provide representative prompt set (500 queries) and expected outputs for quality checks - due 2026-09-11
Evan - Provision test VPC with additional memory for KV cache and enable metrics export to Grafana - due 2026-09-12
Marta - Create dashboard tile for per-route cache hit/miss and store in shared drive - due 2026-09-13
next_steps: Samir to email PulseHealth the cache tuning doc + sample scripts (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/cache-tuning)
Run prefix-only benchmark (Lena) and share raw logs + Grafana link
Customer to send 500-query prompt corpus for quality evaluation
Schedule technical deep-dive next Wednesday to review benchmark results and any hallucination/regression signals
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we said 45 mins, we'll focus on cache numbers and the tuning plan. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:07] Rajiv: Rajiv here, ML eng, ready.
[00:09] Sofia: Sofia, product.
[00:10] Evan: Evan, infra.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, CTO.
[00:13] Lena: Lena from Redwood, hi. Marta: Marta, hi.
[00:15] Samir: Cool, okay, jumping in. I shared the dashboard earlier - top-line: prefix cache hit is at about 23% today, KV cache sits around 58%. Those are across the pilot traffic from last week.
[00:28] Rajiv: Yeah those numbers match what we saw internally; surprised prefix is so low. A lot of our requests include user-specific IDs in the prompt so maybe that's leaking through.
[00:36] Lena: That makes sense, prefix caching benefits from stable system prompts and template parts. If user IDs or session tokens are embedded, keys get unique. We should canonicalize the prompts and strip or replace variable parts.
[00:47] Sofia: Curious - what parts exactly are in prefix vs KV for you? We currently send a system message + user message + optional context pulled from patient records (PII stripped but still variable).
[00:58] Marta: Quick note, our instrumentation groups the initial system message as prefix, the rest goes to KV, but there's some overlap. The auto-keying sometimes uses raw tokens which can be brittle.
[01:10] Evan: We're worried about caching affecting correctness - if we increase cache aggressiveness could we see regressions/hallucinations?
[01:18] Lena: Good question. In practice, caching prefixes that are deterministic (like system + standard instructions) is safe; caching KV entries that include patient history is riskier. We recommend conservative TTLs, and quality evals against the prompt corpus before enabling broad caching.
[01:31] Samir: Right - our baseline proposal: normalize prompts (strip IDs, canonicalize whitespace, map synonyms), then compute cache keys from the normalized prefix+system only. For KV, increase capacity but keep shorter TTL (24h) and monitor.
[01:44] Rajiv: Can you give concrete numbers from the experiment last week?
[01:47] Lena: Yeah - last run (09/01) had prefix hit 23%, KV hit 58%. Token-level latency median was ~210ms, p95 ~520ms. When we forced prefix-only caching in a small test, median dropped to 170ms and cost per 1k tokens down ~12%, but KV cold starts still hit sometimes causing spikes.
[02:10] Priya: That p95 is concerning for SLAs - what's the main cause of spikes?
[02:14] Marta: Mostly KV cache misses combined with model cold-starts when we route to a different node due to autoscale. Also some inefficiencies from key sharding.
[02:22] Samir: Two levers: improve key reuse (so more hits) and increase steady-state KV capacity to reduce evictions; plus revisit autoscale timing to avoid mid-request node churn.
[02:31] Evan: We can provision a larger KV memory on the test cluster; cost is ok for pilot.
[02:36] Rajiv: For canonicalization, we can provide a list of variable tokens (IDs, timestamps). Might be tricky for natural language fields.
[02:43] Lena: We usually apply rule-based extraction first: regexes for IDs, dates, numeric tokens, then a shallow semantic dedup that maps common paraphrases to canonical forms. It isn't perfect - we expect some noise.
[02:54] Samir: Also suggestion: use prompt templates on the client side so the variable slots are explicit, e.g., {{patient_name}} replaced with placeholder before sending to Redwood. That dramatically increases prefix reuse.
[03:06] Sofia: That would require product changes; doable but needs timeline.
[03:10] Priya: How much improvement could we expect if we did client-side templating?
[03:13] Lena: In similar pilots we saw prefix hit jump from ~25% to 65-75% after template adoption. KV hit also improves since fewer unique keys are generated.
[03:23] Rajiv: That's optimistic but promising. Any downsides?
[03:26] Marta: Main downside is engineering work to change request formation; and you have to be careful about privacy - do not put raw PII into cacheable prefixes.
[03:34] Samir: We'll produce a canonicalization script you can run server-side if client changes are slow. It's best-effort but reduces engineering lift.
[03:42] Rajiv: Good. For TTL values what are you recommending?
[03:44] Lena: For prefix: long TTLs (7d+) since they are deterministic. For KV: start with 24h, evaluate, then expand to 72h if not causing stale outputs. Also set a soft LRU bias for recent items.
[03:57] Evan: Any support for selective invalidation? We might want to purge keys when a patient's record updates.
[04:03] Marta: Yes we support explicit key invalidation via API; you'll need to surface events from your system to call Redwood's invalidate endpoint. We can provide a webhook pattern.
[04:11] Priya: Let's talk benchmark plan - what do you want us to run?
[04:15] Lena: We propose two controlled runs: (A) prefix-only caching with prompt canonicalization applied (server-side script), and (B) prefix + expanded KV capacity with 24h TTL. Each run should be 2 hours of mixed traffic (we recommend using your 500-query sample repeated with jitter). We'll capture hit rates, latency, token costs, and quality diffs.
[04:38] Rajiv: We'll provide the 500-query set. Do you need ground truth outputs?
[04:42] Samir: Yes, please provide expected outputs for the 500 queries or at least pass/fail criteria for critical questions. We'll run automated quality checks (BLEU-ish / exact match for template answers) and spot manual review for open-ended outputs.
[04:55] Sofia: On dashboards - can you add per-route cache metrics?
[04:59] Marta: Yep, we'll add a Grafana tile showing per-route prefix/KV hit rates and per-token cost. We'll share read-only links.
[05:06] Evan: For the KV capacity increase, how much more memory do you recommend?
[05:10] Lena: Start with +30% memory for KV shards; observe eviction rate. If eviction drops <5% and hit rates improve, that's good.
[05:18] Priya: Any security concerns with longer TTLs? We need to ensure everything encrypted at rest and in transit and that cache data is isolated per-tenant.
[05:26] Samir: Absolutely - Redwood uses tenant-isolated namespaces for KV, encryption at rest, and supports KMS integration. We'll attach SOC2 pack and our KMS architecture notes after the call.
[05:36] Rajiv: Can you send the sample canonicalization script?
[05:38] Samir: Yep, I'll send that and the doc.
[05:40] Lena: One more thing - we noticed a small bug in our key-sharding logic can cause slightly uneven distribution on low-traffic tenants. We've patched it in the staging runtime; we'll enable the patch for the pilot cluster before the benchmark. Expected effect: smoother KV evictions.
[05:53] Rajiv: Nice.
[05:54] Samir: Ok recapping next steps - Samir send docs & scripts; Lena run benchmarks and share results; Rajiv provide 500 queries and expected outputs; Evan provision test cluster changes; Marta create dashboards. We'll reconvene next Wednesday for results review.
[06:10] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:12] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links. Bye.

Notes: transcription contains a few misheard terms (e.g., "KV cash" heard once), occasional speaker mislabels earlier in the call.
